Studies use complementary controls. [Woolridge et al.](https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-2955/paper8.pdf) shuffle training histories while preserving validation/test targets, testing order beyond history content. [Siciliano et al.](https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3924/paper1.pdf) remove interactions at different positions and measure ranking changes, finding strong last-item dependence; deletion, however, can also change length and positional assignments. [Spotify’s benchmark study](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) compares last-item Markov models, recency-weighted pairwise models, and Transformers, separating predictive gains from last-item transitions, older-history evidence, and joint contextualization.

Fixed-length replacement controls appear in [Xu et al.](https://csr21.github.io/xu-csr2021.pdf), which uses learned history distributions rather than unrestricted random replacements to improve plausibility. The reviewed sources do not establish joint frequency-and-embedding-norm matching as standard practice. Recommended extension: replace one item at a fixed position using training-frequency and learned-norm matches; preserve padding, timestamps, candidates, and repetition status. Compare swaps preserving the item multiset, shuffles preserving the last item, and last-item-only baselines. Stratify repeated versus unique items. Vary absolute position independently of distance from the sequence end where feasible. Matching reduces confounding but cannot guarantee realistic transitions; compare random replacements with context-compatible alternatives and report replacement variability.

[SASRec’s original implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec) trains on next-item targets throughout training sequences. Consequently, probing prediction of final training interactions measures sensitivity on fitted examples and may reflect memorization; it does not establish generalizable temporal dependence. Recommended control: report those diagnostics separately from perturbations predicting untouched validation targets, with paired users/candidates and uncertainty estimates. Strong training-only effects should remain evidence of fitted-model sensitivity, not temporal generalization or causal user preferences.
